answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded escrow and treats correlated equivocation across k coordinated identities as pairwise fault evidence, imposing O(k²) penalties rather than k independent fines. Detection compounds the slash through an exponential capital-loss multiplier, so splitting stake into a swarm raises, rather than dilutes, expected cost. This makes a voyage through shale-like uncertainty safer for honest validators, while a grove of colluding keys risks rapid depletion of its bonded capital.
